lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record--For the Appellant. 

Shafiq Ahmed, Senior Advocate (Tabarak Hossain, Advocate with him) instructed by AKM Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record---For the Respondent No. 1. 

Respondent Nos. 2-6---Not Represented.
parties:
Ruhul Amin ------ Appellant
vs
Official Liquidator, Mahaluxmi Bank Ltd ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J: This appeal by leave, at the instance of the proforma defendant No. 6, is directed against the judgment and order dated 9-5-1984 of the High Court Division passed in Suit No. 1 of 1981 decreeing the suit upon declaring that the property described in the schedule of the plaint belonged to Mahaluxmi Bank Ltd (in liquidation), the bank, and that the defendants have no right, title or interest in the land in suit, the registered deed of sale No. 5870 dated 29-9-1958 executed by Madhabi Lata Lala in favour of the defendant No. 2, only insofar sale of the suit plot is concerned, is null and void, the bank would be entitled to recover khas possession of the suit property by evicting the defendants and removing structures from the suit property except the defendant No. 4, who shall pay to the bank such sum as may be determined by the Court on an application to be filed by the Officer Liquidator of this bank or the said defendant No. 4 to perfect its title to that portion of the suit property which is in its occupation and the said defendant may recover his said sum from defendant Nos. 1 and 3 and the defendant Nos. 1, 5 and 6 may negotiate with the Official Liquidator of the bank for realisation of possession of those parts of the suit property which are in their possession on payment of such sum as may be agreed upon subject to the approval of the Court upon an application by either the Official Liquidator or the defendant Nos. 1, 5 and 6 to be concluded within 1 year from the date of drawing up of the order of the Court failing which the official Liquidator would be at liberty to execute the instant order of the Court. 

 2. The respondent No. 1, the Official Liquidator of the bank, filed the above suit seeking declaration that the suit property belongs to the bank and the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the same and that if the suit property or part thereof is found to be not in possession of the bank then restore possession of the same in its favour on the averments that Sarada Kripa Lala was the owner of the suit property, that is RS Plot No. 2956 in RS Khatian No. 776 corresponding to CS Plot No. 1748 (Part under CS Khatian No. 41 comprising 8.81 acres of land of Mouza East Nasirabad, Chittagong and he, in the year 1929, as security against loans granted to him by the bank, mortgaged the same with the bank along with his other properties, by way of depositing of title deeds and also delivering the possession of the suit property to the bank; then the bank filed an application for mutation of the suit property along with other properties and the Khashmahal Tahsilder, Sadar, Chittagong by order dated 7-1-36 passed in Judicial Miscellaneous (JM) Case No. 236 of 1936-37 mutated the name of the bank in the suit property; Sarada Kripa Lala having failed to repay the loans, the bank filed mortgage suit and obtaining decree filed Mortgage Execution Case No. 51 of 1952 and therein purchased the suit property along with other mortgaged properties; one Haroon Matin filed Money Suit No. 5 of 1957 against the bank claiming Taka 21,000 as damages stating that he, along with Allah Rakha Bai, took lease of the suit property as well as six other plots from the bank for 99 years and subsequently it transpired that the bank had no title on the properties leased to them and the bank, by misrepresentation, leased the same to them and then on obtaining decree dated 14-2-1959 in the above suit, Haroon Matin filed Money Execution Case No. 25 of 1959 wherein he, in collusion with the  then officials of the bank, managed to auction purchase the suit property as well as other six plots in the name of his father, the defendant No. 2; after the bank was wound up by order dated 18-3-1960, the Official Liquidator of the bank filed Pauper Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1960 to set aside the above auction sale of the properties of the bank which, subsequently being transferred to the High Court, Dhaka in terms of section 61 of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, was renumbered as Transferred Suit No. 1 of 1981 and, after hearing, the High Court, Dhaka, by judgment and order dated 22-12-1966, decreed the suit declaring the above leases in favour of Haroon Matin and another as well as the subsequent auction purchase of the suit property in the name of defendant No. 2 in Money Execution Case No. 25 of 1959 as null and void with the observation that the officials of the bank, who were in charge of the litigation, had colluded with Haroon Matin. As against that, Haroon Matin filed Letters Patent Appeal No. 4 of 1967 and a Division Bench of the High Court Dhaka by judgment and order dated 31-3-1977 dismissed the above appeal. 

 3. Then Haroon Matin filed Civil Appeal No. 16 of 1979 and the Appellate Division, after hearing, taking into consideration of the provisions of section 73 of the Banking Companies Act 1962 and the case of Official Receiver vs Das Bank Ltd reported in 27 DLR (AD) 133 by judgment and order dated 25-6-80 upheld the above judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 31-1-1977 with the observation that "there can be no doubt that the leases forming parts of the same transaction by fraud and collusion will fall together being void ab initio"; then during spot verification of the suit property in the year 1980 the Official Liquidator came to know that both the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title in the suit property and litigations are pending; further in reply to the query made by the Official Liquidator to the defendant No. 1 regarding the basis of his claim, the defendant No. 1 by his letter dated 28-11-80 informed the Official Liquidator that in the year 1907 Apparna Charan, his father, took lease of CS Plot No. 1748 from Sadar Khashmahal, Chittagong and the relevant documents of the above lease have been filed by him in the High Court Division in connection with the aforesaid First Appeal No. 115 of 1965. Further case of the bank was, that the suit property being requisitioned in LA Case No. 62/1942-43 during Second World War was taken over for use of the military but later on was derequisitioned on 12-12-1946, and possession was handed over to the bank on 20-1-1947 and that although the defendant No. 1 in his letter dated 28th November, 1980 claimed title over the suit property tracing back his title from the year 1907 but from the records it will be evident that the suit property was owned by Sarada Kripa Lala as recorded owner till 6th November, 1936 and thereafter the same was owned by the bank and that the defendant No. 1, without serving any notice upon the bank, got the suit property mutated in his name in JM Case No. 230A/11 of 1954-55. 

 4. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1 and proforma defendant No. 6 who filed joint affidavit in opposition contending, inter alia, that the suit property actually appertained to original Jote No. 88/88 of Mouza East Nasirabad, which was created in Settlement Case No. 284 of 1907-1908 in favour of Aparna Charan, the father of the defendant No. 1, and the said jote comprised the lands of CS Plot Nos. 1609, 1736 and 1748 and on 29-11-1912 Aparna Charan, filed an application before the Khashmahal Office for demarcation of the said jote land which was registered as Judicial Miscellaneous Case (JM Case) No. 288 of 1911-12 and order was passed therein on 26-3-1912 for demarcation of the lands settled in favour of Aparna Charan and accordingly, demarcation was made by an Amin of the said office on 26-3-1912 and since the creation of the said jote Aparna Charan had been in exclusive possession of the suit property and he had brick fields therein as well as the adjoining lands and during RS operation major portion of the said Jote No. 88/88 was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 as RS Jote No. 81 and by mistake the remaining portion, i.e. the suit property comprising of RS Plot No, 2956 appertaining to RS Khatian No. 776, was wrongly recorded in the name of Sarada Kripa Lala as RS Jote No. 86 though he had no title or possession therein and that the defendant No. 1, after death of his father in the year 1929, had also been in continuous possession thereof over the statutory period of limitation and also used the suit land as a part of his brick field and after coming to know that the bank wrongly entered its name in the RS record in JM Case No. 236 of 1936-37, filed an application praying for mutation of his name upon correction of the aforesaid wrong entry in the name of the bank and the said application to the Khashmohal Office, Sadar, Chittagong, was registered as JM Case No. 230A/11 of 1554-55 and then notice was duly served upon the bank and in spite of receiving the notice the bank, having no interest in the suit property, did not contest the said application and then the right, title, interest and possession of the defendant No. 1 being found in Jote No. 86 after proper enquiry, by order dated 30-3-1955 the suit property, along with other properties, were recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 and as far back as 1959 he sold a part of the suit land measuring 1.20 acres to Pakistan Tobacco Co Ltd, the predecessor in interest of Bangladesh Tobacco Co Ltd, the defendant No. 3, who after enjoying the said property till 1964 disposed of the same in favour of State Bank of Pakistan, the predecessor of Bangladesh Bank, the defendant No. 4, whose name has been duly recorded in the record of rights and who is in possession of the same by paying rents regularly; the defendant No. 5 is in possession of part of the suit property by virtue of his purchase from a subsequent transferee of the defendant No. 1 and the proforma defendant No. 6 is in possession of part of the suit property by virtue of direct purchase from the defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 1 has made similar transfers from the suit property to various other purchasers and they, after constructing pucca buildings on portions of the suit property so purchased are in possession of the same long over the statutory period of limitation openly and adversely and since they were not made parties, the suit is bad for defect of parties and neither Sarada Kripa Lala nor the bank had ever any possession, right, title or interest in the suit property. 

 5. The defendant No. 2 also contested the suit and filed separate affidavit-in-opposition contending that Sarada Kripa Lala never mortgaged the suit property to the bank the suit property did not become the subject matter of the mortgage suit as well as the execution case and that the suit property was rightly recorded in the name of Sarada Kripa Lala during RS operation wherein his status has been recorded as a sthitiban raiyat and he on 4-3-29, made a will bequeathing the suit jote to Madhabi Lata Lala, his daughter-in-law, who, on 17-12-1940 after obtaining probate in Probate Suit No. 4 of 1939 was in continuous and uninterrupted possession of the same on payment of rent and she, after obtaining per-mission from the concerned authority under section 9 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and also obtaining Income Tax Clearance Certificates, sold the suit jote to the defendant No. 2 by kabala dated 29-9-1958 and thus the defendant No. 2 became the absolute owner in possession of the suit jote and his title has also been perfected by lapse of time and that the defendant No. 1, having fraudulently got his name mutated in RS Jote No. 86 and resisted the mutation of the name of this defendant and also the possession of the defendant No. 2 in the suit jote, he filed Other Class Suit No. 49 of  1959 for declaration of his title in the suit jote and also for recovery of khas possession which being dismissed he preferred First Appeal No. 115 of 1965 before the High Court, Dhaka which is pending. 

 "Thus it is clear that the Bank itself was under a mistaken belief that it was a mortgagee in possession in respect of RS Jote No. 86. It's application in respect of RS Jote No. 86 for mutation was founded on that behalf. The Khashmohal also granted the Bank's prayer in the way it wanted. But in actual fact there was no mortgage of RS Jote No. 86. The application for mutation as a mortgagee in possession was a mistaken application. The actual mutation was a mortgagee in possession does not also reflect the correct position. The correct possession is that the Bank entered into possession of RS Jote No. 86 mistakenly as a mortgagee."
